title: Time & dates
intro: Read a clock, distinguish a time from a duration, navigate an example calendar and tell a day in order. The source date is 3 November 2026; daypart boundaries are flexible.

terms.en: two in these clock-hour and measure phrases
day of the month in conversation
day in formal or written dates
the third day of the month

examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang shíyī diǎn zuǒyòu, wǒ shàngchuáng shuìjiào.
examples.en: Around 11 P.M., I go to bed.

topics.title: Ask and build a time
topics.explanation: Daypart + hour + 点 + minutes. Time normally precedes the activity. These examples use 8:40 in the morning.
topics.visualIntent: Clock at 8:40 with an interpolated hour hand; assemble daypart/hour/minutes.

topics.title: Eight everyday clocks
topics.explanation: Watch both hands. 一刻 is fifteen minutes, 半 is thirty, 三刻 is forty-five. At 8:45, 差一刻九点 is another way to say a quarter to nine.
topics.visualIntent: Eight source clock presets with movable hands and minute controls; 12/24-hour wording.

topics.title: Parts of the day
topics.explanation: The band is illustrative. Dayparts overlap: 早上 and 上午 can overlap, and 中午 is around noon. They are not exact legal boundaries. Formal timetables can use 24-hour numbers; conversation usually uses a daypart.
topics.visualIntent: An approximate 24-hour day/night band linked to eight daypart examples.

topics.title: Clock point or duration?
topics.explanation: A point on a clock answers when; an interval answers how long. 分 is used in clock readings, 分钟 for a duration. These examples use 两点 and 两个小时, but 二十 means twenty.
topics.visualIntent: Side-by-side clock point and interval bar; selectable duration lengths, not interchangeable labels.

topics.title: Before, after and around
topics.explanation: 以前 and 以后 locate something before/after a reference. 左右 and 大概 express approximation. 从…到… marks an interval; 然后 links the next event.
topics.visualIntent: Reference at eight with before/after positions; a fuzzy region around seven; interval from eight to twelve.

topics.title: Read a date
topics.explanation: Use year → month → day. Read a year digit by digit. 号 is conversational and 日 is formal/written. This source example is Tuesday, 3 November 2026, not a live claim about today.
topics.visualIntent: Monday-first November 2026 calendar with Tuesday 3 highlighted; navigate practice dates without treating source date as device today.

topics.title: Days, weeks and months
topics.explanation: Month names use a number + 月. 星期日 and 星期天 both mean Sunday. Relative words need a reference day, week or month.
topics.visualIntent: Selectable practice calendar plus yesterday/today/tomorrow/day-after strip; names and weekday/date remain consistent.

topics.title: A morning in order
topics.explanation: This is the PDF’s separate around-seven example, not an edit to your existing My Day lesson. Follow the order; untimed actions do not acquire invented exact times.
topics.visualIntent: Ordered morning events: around seven is approximate; the walk has a ten-minute duration; other actions stay untimed.

topics.title: Class times and breaks
topics.explanation: Use exact class anchors and measured breaks. 10:10 → 10:30 is twenty minutes; noon → 13:00 is one hour. The seven o’clock morning and this schedule belong to this source only.
topics.visualIntent: A full-day schedule with exact class times, measured breaks, and untimed home activities kept untimed.

topics.title: Recall, writing and IME choices
topics.explanation: Hide the model before answering. Tone marks or tone numbers are accepted in pinyin checks. Untoned IME strings admit both candidates; meaning and context decide which you intend.
topics.visualIntent: Contextual IME contrasts dian/shi/yue/hao and ten exact pinyin-recall source targets; supported handwriting of 点分时间年月号前后.
